name: Snatch Balance
description: The snatch balance is an Olympic weightlifting accessory exercise in which the bar is taken from the back rack position and the athlete uses a dip-and-drive to push themselves under the bar into a full overhead squat. It trains the speed of the third pull (turning the hands over and dropping under the bar) and reinforces the ability to stabilize a heavy snatch catch. The snatch balance is typically performed with higher loads than the actual snatch to overload the catch position.

execution.starting_position: Bar across the back in a high bar squat position, with a wide snatch grip. Feet in squat stance.
execution.setup_instructions: Take the bar from a rack with a wide snatch grip. The dip-and-drop is key — practice with an empty bar first.
steps: Step 1: Hold the bar on the back in a wide snatch grip, feet in squat stance.
Step 2: Dip the knees 10–15 cm with a vertical torso.
Step 3: Drive the bar upward slightly while simultaneously pressing yourself under the bar.
Step 4: Rotate the hands and punch the bar overhead into a locked overhead squat position.
Step 5: Stabilize in the full overhead squat, then stand.
execution.breathing_instructions: Brace before the dip. Exhale after stabilizing overhead.
common_mistakes: Pressing the bar up high before dropping under — the goal is to use minimal upward force and mainly drop
Insufficient ankle or shoulder mobility causing the squat to collapse
safety_considerations: This exercise requires excellent shoulder and ankle mobility. Use a rack with safeties.
Be prepared to drop the bar safely forward.
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full overhead squat depth with locked-out bar position.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Explosive dip-drive. Fast hands. Stable catch before standing.
coaching_cues: Dip straight — drive the bar up slightly, then drop fast
Punch the hands up and lock out
